-111.89593,33.37795.name: Tao of Women Clinic
-111.89593,33.37795.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

77.59008,12.97679.name: Adgyl Lifesciences Private Limited
77.59008,12.97679.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.10876,51.38913.name: Croydon University Hospital
-0.10876,51.38913.state: Fertility Centre, 530 London Road, Thornton Heath, CR7 7YE
-0.10876,51.38913.company: Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic Bromley
-0.10876,51.38913.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic Bromley. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-0.13000,51.52300.name: Understanding Animal Research
-0.13000,51.52300.state: London — Abbey House, 74-76 St John St
-0.13000,51.52300.desc: A UK organisation that publishes animal-use figures and runs the Concordat under which research institutions commit to openness about what they do. It is industry-funded advocacy and it is also the reason the UK has some of the most detailed public animal-use data anywhere — both facts are true, and the data is checkable regardless of who paid for the campaign.

-4.02000,5.32000.name: Conseil du Café-Cacao
-4.02000,5.32000.desc: Côte d’Ivoire produces more cocoa than anywhere else, grown almost entirely by smallholders, and the crop faces a virus conventional breeding has not solved. What happens to cocoa genetics is decided between this board, the chocolate companies and the research collections — and the growers are the party with the least say and the most at stake.

4.38100,50.84800.name: European Research Council
4.38100,50.84800.desc: Funds investigator-led research across the EU on scientific merit alone, and is the main European source for the basic work that later becomes a platform. Emmanuelle Charpentier's CRISPR work was ERC-funded, which is why a European public grant sits behind a patent estate now licensed worldwide.
